newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian liquidity tighter as franc weakens.
newsitem.headline: Belgian liquidity tighter as franc weakens.

text.p: Belgian money market liquidity was tighter and short-term rates up to one month edged higher as the Belgian franc stubbornly remained above the 20.64 to the mark level in early trade on Friday.
Dealers said they saw no reason why the franc would not go to its 20.6255 ERM pivot rate, and added that the central bank was gradually raising the price of money.
Dealers said the bank was giving liquidity at repo rates around 3.09 percent, from 3.07 earlier this week, and that even at 3.09 percent bidders were not getting all the funds they wanted.
"There seems to be some liquidity shortage, which is worsened by people's anticipations," one dealer said.
By 0815 the franc was quoted at 20.6400/10 to the mark from 20.6408/17 Thursday and after having dipped below 20.64 at the start.
The Belgian futures and options exchange Belfox' new medium-term future contract BMBc1 got off to a slow start. Only 11 lots were traded after an hour and a half of trade.
Dealers were cool on the contract, saying it came to late to become a succes. "Soon we will have the Euro and we'll all trade Bund futures," one said.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
